articleTitle: SpecC design environment
publicationTitle: 2001 IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems (ISCAS)
abstract: The author discusses the SpecC design environment, considering the following topics: validation levels; abstraction levels; SpecC scope, methodology and refinements; refinement user interface; user feedback; user guided refinement; automatic refinement; validation user interface; modelling, refinement, exploration and synthesis engines.

articleTitle: Design of integrated circuits for audiometric applications
publicationTitle: 2001 IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems (ISCAS)
abstract: This article presents integrated circuit design for audiometric applications, including discussions of hearing and hearing defects, audiometric tests and audiometers, signal generators and attenuators and power amplifiers.

articleTitle: Support vector machine learning
publicationTitle: 2001 IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems (ISCAS)

articleTitle: Design of low voltage CMOS circuits
publicationTitle: 2001 IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems (ISCAS)
abstract: This article discusses high performance and low-power circuits. It covers leakage control (CAD and circuit techniques) including stacked CMOS with gated-Vdd (application: DRI-cache), multiple VT and dynamic VT, circuit techniques (MTCMOS, VTCMOS. DTMOS, SCMOS, etc.) and SOI implementation. Ultra low voltage digital sub-threshold logic in bursty and non-bursty modes for medical applications, and testing of deep sub-micron low voltage CMOS (modified IDDQ testing and cross-talk faults in high speed circuits) are also discussed.

articleTitle: Statistical approach and application to EMI reduction - Statistical approach to discrete-time chotic systems: some tools for studying chaos with densities and application to EMI reduction
publicationTitle: 2001 IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems (ISCAS)

articleTitle: Statistical learning and VC theory
publicationTitle: 2001 IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems (ISCAS)
abstract: The article applies statistical learning theory to the supervised learning problem. Pattern recognition is covered, including Vapnik-Chervonenkis (VC) theory and the implications for support vector machines (SVMs), neural networks and decision trees. Real predictions are given for scale-sensitive dimensions. The article concludes by analysing large margin classification.

articleTitle: The SpecC language
publicationTitle: 2001 IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems (ISCAS)
abstract: The SpecC Language is executable and synthesizable and gives precise coverage of system language requirements with orthogonal constructs for orthogonal concepts. SpecC has been adopted in industry and academia with the introduction of the SpecC Open Technology Consortium (STOC). For the future there is a standardization effort in progress by STOC.

articleTitle: Low power and high performance DSPs for mobile wireless communications systems
publicationTitle: 2001 IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems (ISCAS)
abstract: The article discusses 2G and 3G mobile wireless systems and algorithms for mobile wireless baseband processing. Examples of low power DSPs for wireless handsets are covered including TIC54, Lucent 1600 and Lucent 16000. High performance DSPs for wireless infrastructure are also covered including TIC6x, Lucent Starcore and Lucent StarPro. The article concludes with an analysis of future trends in high performance & low power DSPs.

articleTitle: Kernel machine learning: a systems perspective
publicationTitle: 2001 IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems (ISCAS)
abstract: The article presents a systems perspective on kernel machine learning, including a discussion of margin and generalization, support vector machines and kernels. Cost functions and dual formulation are covered including classification, regression and probability estimation. The article concludes by analysing sparsity, incremental learning and learning machines.

articleTitle: Design principles for low-voltage low-power analog integrated circuits
publicationTitle: 2001 IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems (ISCAS)
abstract: Design strategies for analog integrated circuits for the reduction of stochastic errors and systematic errors are normally not consistent with design strategies which take into account power dissipation, voltage range and current range. The combination of transfer quality, low voltage and low power must be considered during the whole design process.

articleTitle: Next generation wireless networks
publicationTitle: 2001 IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems (ISCAS)
abstract: The authors discuss next generation wireless networks, covering the following topics: the evolution of the mobile network; the GRPS network architecture and protocols; the CDMA1X and HDR networks; the WCDMA network architecture and protocol stack; all-IP networks. architecture. Mobile networks are deploying infrastructure to provide a high speed data capability. As these next generation of networks are deployed a new generation of services will be deployed on cellular networks. Backbone networks are converging based on IP as a common networking layer. Thus the wireless network will simply be an extension of this new network.

articleTitle: Introduction to 3G/4G wireless network architectures
publicationTitle: 2001 IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems (ISCAS)
abstract: The author presents a general discussion on 3G and 4G wireless network architectures. The topics covered include: the basic features of 3G and 4G systems; the migration path from 2G to 3G and 4G; service characteristics; the wireless networking environment; radio transmission issues; the air interface issue; transmission techniques; software radio; and Bluetooth.

articleTitle: VLSI scaling trends and challenges
publicationTitle: 2001 IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems (ISCAS)
abstract: This article discusses trends in VLSI technology evolution. It concentrates on challenges to VLSI scaling, including transistor scaling, interconnect scaling, leakage currents and silicon-on-insulator technology. It concludes that we still have not found a fundamental barrier to extending Moore's law and that the major challenge to scaling in the future will be power and efficiency.

articleTitle: Circuit techniques for high speed communication
publicationTitle: 2001 IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems (ISCAS)
abstract: This article analyses the technology limits for designing integrated circuits for high-speed communication applications. It includes discussions on channel and protocol processing and CMOS circuit techniques.

articleTitle: Modeling and design with SpecC
publicationTitle: 2001 IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems (ISCAS)
abstract: Discusses system design and SpecC design methodology. Specification model, architecture model, communication model and implementation model realisations are implemented.

articleTitle: Design of a JBIG encoder with SpecC methodology
publicationTitle: 2001 IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems (ISCAS)
abstract: JBIG is an image compression standard. It is distortionless and uses progressive encoding. SpecC methodology is demonstrated with a real example. SpecC is capable of transforming an executable specification into an RTL implementation. Basic refinement rules are established and applied to transform SpecC models. With the availability of SpecC automated tools, productivity gains of 100/spl times/ are achievable over the manual approach.

articleTitle: Design of a GSM vocoder
publicationTitle: 2001 IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems (ISCAS)
abstract: Describes a UCI - Motorola joint project demonstrating SpecC methodology. Evaluates benefits of enhanced full-rate (EFR) vocoder with GSM standard for mobile telephony (GSM 06.10) and lossy voice encoding/decoding: stream of speech samples at 104 kbit/s; encoded bit stream at 12.2 kbit/s.

articleTitle: First- and second-order oscillators
publicationTitle: 2001 IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems (ISCAS)

articleTitle: An operating point elimination technique for weak-inversion log-domain filters with multiple operating points
publicationTitle: 2001 IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems (ISCAS)

articleTitle: Systematic design of data converters
publicationTitle: 2001 IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems (ISCAS)
abstract: The author discusses the systematic design of data converters. The topics covered include: performance limits in analog designs; data converter design flow; architectural design; circuit design; and layout generation.

articleTitle: Wireless access technologies - tutorial
publicationTitle: 2001 IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems (ISCAS)
abstract: Selection/design of multiple access needs to consider a number of factors. TDMA and CDMA are both capable of supporting packet services e.g. GSM and 3G/UMTS. Packet access puts more concern on the speed of access (channel request and channel allocation); higher layers need to cooperate (i.e. reduce the number of layers) and considerable overhead for access is inevitable.

articleTitle: Interfacing electronic circuits to neural systems
publicationTitle: 2001 IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems (ISCAS)
abstract: The application of electronic systems to restore or assist impaired functions in people with certain types of physical disability is a rapidly expanding area of biomedical engineering. Currently, the most widely used device designed to restore an impaired sensorineural function is the cochlear implant, which has proven to be an effective and safe treatment for many people with severe to profound deafness. Worldwide, there are now well over 30,000 adults and children who use cochlear implants to enhance their ability to communicate using spoken language, and to perceive environmental sounds. The tutorial presented here discusses some of the main issues involved in interfacing electronic circuits to the nervous system, and draws upon the substantial experience gained with cochlear implants over the past few decades for specific, practical examples.

articleTitle: Neuromorphic medical electronics
publicationTitle: 2001 IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems (ISCAS)
abstract: This article discusses neuromorphic medical electronics including biological computation, neuromorphic coding, neuromorphic hardware and neuromorphic instrumentation. Two examples are given from the auditory system: a silicon cochlea and a neuromorphic cochlea implant.

articleTitle: Deep submicron CMOS: Characteristics & circuit design
publicationTitle: 2001 IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems (ISCAS)
abstract: The article presents 0.13 /spl mu/m device properties for CMOS integrated circuits, including transistors and passives. Circuit design principles and characteristics of RF circuits are covered. Circuit techniques for gain stages are also discussed. The article concludes with some technology predictions.

articleTitle: Statistical approach to discrete-time chaotic systems: application of basic and advanced tools to DS-CDMA system optimization
publicationTitle: 2001 IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems (ISCAS)
abstract: Gives an introduction to DS-CDMA systems. Covers DS-CDMA principle (spreading, synchronization), performance overview, advanced receiver structure and classic versus chaotic spreading sequences. Performance on ideal channels is discussed. Cross-interference analysis, (n,t)-tailed shift performance, performance reformulation as a function of self-interference, performance optimization using the self-interference profile and chaotic optimum map search are all included. Performance on selective channels is also looked at.

articleTitle: Supporting flows for high speed design
publicationTitle: 2001 IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems (ISCAS)
abstract: New EDA tools are needed all the time. Old approaches are running out of steam with changing technologies, nonlinear interactions and "new economy" issues. Integration at the flow level is needed i.e. design and library data transport and movement of the "meaning" of the design. The EAMRI program is discussed.

articleTitle: Synchronous optical network (SONET/SDH)
publicationTitle: 2001 IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems (ISCAS)
abstract: This article attempts to provide a comprehensive exposure to SONET/SDH. It explains what SONET is and why it is so important, and the use of SONET terms and acronyms such as STS, SPE, VT, ADM. It also discusses network functions and applications, and addresses the use of self-healing rings.

articleTitle: 100 nm CMOS technology. A design perspective
publicationTitle: 2001 IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems (ISCAS)
abstract: This article discusses the design of 100 nm CMOS integrated circuits, emphasising the implications for transistors, logic circuits, matching techniques and embedded systems. Included is a discussion of the requirements of high-speed low-power circuits, and the emerging system-on-chip technologies.

articleTitle: Dynamics of microwave FET behaviour
publicationTitle: 2001 IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems (ISCAS)
abstract: The article discusses dispersion in the dynamic characteristics of microwave HEMTs, and the application of a pulsed-bias measurement system. Thermal effects and non-thermal effects are analysed.

articleTitle: The future of semiconductors; Moore or less
publicationTitle: 2001 IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems (ISCAS)
abstract: Scaling results in: increasing design productivity gap; increasing mask costs; increasing leakage currents; increasing noise while noise margins reduce; increasing test costs; increasing technology costs due to approaching the limits. Design measures to limit leakage and noise and to support testing and debug, require an increasing number of transistors (up to 20-40%) and more complex processes to support embedded options. The move to the next technology will become less and less commercially attractive.

articleTitle: ISCAS2001 tutorial/short course & special session on high speed devices & modelling
publicationTitle: 2001 IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems (ISCAS)
abstract: This tutorial presents an introduction to large-signal models for high-speed devices. It analyses nonlinear charge and capacitance models and introduces black-box behavioral modeling.

articleTitle: Microwave circuits
publicationTitle: 2001 IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems (ISCAS)

articleTitle: Signal processing techniques for optical transceivers
publicationTitle: 2001 IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems (ISCAS)
abstract: This article presents signal processing techniques for optical transceivers, including a discussion of optical channel impairments. Fiber equalization is covered including DSP-based detection and analog equalization for 10 Gb/s and beyond. The article concludes with an analysis of forward error correction for low-power high-performance applications.

articleTitle: Factors for success in SoC design
publicationTitle: 2001 IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems (ISCAS)
abstract: The author discusses the various factors which should be taken into account for the successful design of a system-on-chip (SoC). These factors result from the merging of software and hardware disciplines and include: the use of the SpecC to implement quickly and easily executable specification and behavioral description creation; the productivity gain from working at higher levels of abstraction; IP reuse; architectural exploration performed quickly and products produced to specification; customers should quickly receive functional models and verify end systems, before costly changes are required.

articleTitle: SpecC Technology Open Consortium
publicationTitle: 2001 IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems (ISCAS)
abstract: Discusses the SpecC Technology Open Consortium which involves product planners and industrial designers for embedded systems, IT designers, embedded software designers, factory automation software designers, system architects, and LSI architecture designers. The aims of the Consortium include the following: specification description language standardisation; establishment of interoperability among design tools; promotion of industry-wide collaboration; establishment of design methodology/guidelines based on SpecC; the easy tailoring of design solutions for each application segments; aggregation and reuse of design IPs.

articleTitle: An analog fully implantable, micropower, log-domain cochlear prosthesis
publicationTitle: 2001 IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems (ISCAS)
abstract: The article presents a power up and AC simulation of a log-domain filter with automatic gain control, current limiting and power level detection for applications in a cochlear prosthesis.

articleTitle: Structured electronic design of bandgap references
publicationTitle: 2001 IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems (ISCAS)
abstract: The authors discuss the design of bandgap references. Firstly they define a bandgap reference as a voltage reference of which the output voltage is referred to the bandgap energy of the used semiconductor. Then they present a systematic design approach, which covers architectures, noise power and supply rejection. A design example is given.

articleTitle: Emerging pervasive technologies for e-commerce
publicationTitle: 2001 IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems (ISCAS)
abstract: The author discusses the emerging technologies for electronic commerce, widely known as e-commerce. The following topics were covered: platforms; wireless communication infrastructure; the short message service (SMS); the IEEE 802.11 standard; HomeRF; UMTS/IMT-2000; software defined radio; and location based technologies.

articleTitle: Low-voltage ultra-low-power analog IC design dynamic translinear circuits
publicationTitle: 2001 IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems (ISCAS)

articleTitle: Pervasive commerce infrastructures and case studies
publicationTitle: 2001 IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems (ISCAS)
abstract: The author discusses pervasive commerce infrastructures and presents some case studies. The topics covered include the wireless access protocol (WAP); the emerging e-commerce infrastructure; space-time tradeoff for pervasive data/media access; and the pervasive e-commerce infrastructure.

articleTitle: Switched-MOSFET sampled-data technique for low-voltage supply
publicationTitle: 2001 IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems (ISCAS)
abstract: This article presents switched-MOSFET (SM) sampled-data circuits designed for a low-voltage supply. It discusses the basic SM cell, SM integrators and universal SM biquads.

articleTitle: Interfacing electronic circuits to neural systems
publicationTitle: 2001 IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems (ISCAS)

articleTitle: Statistical approach to discrete-time chaotic systems: advanced tools for quantized chaotic trajectories
publicationTitle: 2001 IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems (ISCAS)
abstract: Classical tools for statistical analysis of chaotic maps can be generalized to express any-order joint probability of the state and thus any-order correlation functions of the trajectories. When trajectories are quantized correlations can be naturally expressed as combinations of tensors. These expressions feature noteworthy properties when,. piecewise-affine Markov maps are considered. The class of (n,t)-tailed shifts spans the range of maps producing exponentially vanishing correlation and allows the derivation of an analytical expression for any-order quantized correlation functions.

articleTitle: ISCAS2001 tutorial/short course & special session on high speed devices & modelling
publicationTitle: 2001 IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems (ISCAS)
abstract: This tutorial presents an introduction to large-signal models for high-speed devices, including nonlinear charge and capacitance modeling and black-box behavioral modeling.

articleTitle: Understanding the emerging and future communications technologies
publicationTitle: 2001 IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems (ISCAS)
abstract: The aim of this tutorial is to understand the key emerging communications technologies in today's communications marketplace. It provides a system level overview of networking technologies that are big winners in the marketplace, explores the SONET/SDH and DWDM evolution, and attempts to understand the vision of Fast and Gigabit Ethernet networks.

articleTitle: Measuring and characterizing devices
publicationTitle: 2001 IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems (ISCAS)

articleTitle: Distortion and intermodulation mechanisms
publicationTitle: 2001 IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems (ISCAS)

articleTitle: Dense wavelength division multiplexing
publicationTitle: 2001 IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems (ISCAS)
abstract: This article provides an introduction to dense wavelength division multiplexing (DWDM) technology and to DWDM communications systems. It presents a comprehensive exposure to WDM and DWDM, explains the major components in optical networks and discusses optical long-haul network functions and applications.

articleTitle: Circuit design techniques for deep submicron technologies
publicationTitle: 2001 IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems (ISCAS)
abstract: This article presents design techniques for deep submicron integrated circuits. It includes a discussion of both chip-level design challenges (capacitive and inductive noise, domino vs. static design styles, dual V/sub T/ transistors and clock distribution) and system-level design challenges.

articleTitle: Gigabit Ethernet
publicationTitle: 2001 IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems (ISCAS)
abstract: This article provides a history of Ethernet (Gigabit Ethernet vs. other technologies) and an overview of the High Speed LAN Technologies. It presents an evaluation of current networking trends, applications and needs. Included is an overview of 10Mb/s Ethernet and Fast Ethernet, the use of Ethernet terms and acronyms such as 10Base-T and VLAN and Gigabit Ethernet's applicability to fulfil market needs. It discusses the Gigabit Ethernet technologies and the 80/20 rule (20% of all traffic is in the backbone and 80% is local).

articleTitle: Tutorial Guide. ISCAS 2001. IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems (Cat. No.01TH8573)
publicationTitle: 2001 IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems (ISCAS)
abstract: Presents the front cover or splash screen of the proceedings record.
